_comment: The first matching profile wins. Key: x_rizzo.fingerprint, then model, then host. A calibrated profile goes AT THE TOP, with match.fingerprint. Per-question entries apply only when the sha256 of the sent text matches. On a question with a fit the decisions stay on the raw value against the policy's threshold, which is shown moved through the fit (calibration.ts), so a fit changes no verdict; an explicit thresholds block in a calibrated profile replaces the policy's value, compared on the calibrated scale, except where a project's rule is stricter, and the plugin's profiles have none. Read only from the user layer or the plugin, never from the project.

profiles.name: spark-bf16-2026-09
profiles.note: The Spark measured on the bench on 2026-09-26 (rizzo-flow, Spark-X2.5-4B BF16): dev set bench/results/2026-09-26-dev-checks (118 diffs) and holdout set 2026-09-26-holdout (121 new diffs), with the checks.json questions tied by per_question.sha256. Calibrated on 2026-09-30 by scripts/fit-calibration.ts (bench/results/2026-09-30-calibration): a Platt per question fitted on the dev set and adopted where a > 0 and it lowers the holdout's log-loss, for seven questions. hardcoded_secret keeps its raw p (the fit made the holdout worse), weakens_expected was not measured on its own labels, and description_matches does not order its labels. The policy's thresholds stay those chosen on the raw p (the _why of each rule) and the decisions stay on the raw value, so every verdict is the raw scale's; what is shown, the value and the threshold moved through the fit, now means what it says, for a mix of problems like the bench's. Temperature 3 for choice and score as in rizzo-provisional: the bench did not measure them. Also valid for a router instance with the same GGUF and the same flags, which has the same fingerprint.

profiles.name: rizzo-provisional
profiles.note: A rizzo with another fingerprint (another GGUF, another llama.cpp build). No Platt scaling on nouls and on choices with a value: a = 1/3 (T≈3, estimated by rizzo-flow on authored144, synthetic English texts rather than diffs) pushed negatives up towards the thresholds (0.02 → 0.22), while the thresholds of policy.json are chosen on the bench's raw p, where the measured wordings give negatives a mean between 0.02 and 0.18. The choice and score temperatures stay, which the bench did not measure. To be replaced by a profile with match.fingerprint and a calibration fit on the Spark.

profiles.name: jev
profiles.note: TypeSafe declares calibrated probabilities: identity. Not verified on diffs.

profiles.name: clm-provisional
profiles.note: CLM (Contrastive-LM, clm-serve): a Qwen3-8B encoder with projection heads, whose answer is a softmax over the question's own options, not a calibrated probability. Not measured on diffs: the thresholds of policy.json come from rizzo and the wide band of an unknown backend applies until a bench run on CLM (bench/MEASUREMENT.md). CLM truncates a state longer than --max-tokens (2048 by default) from the front, with no error: serve it with 4096 (docs/spark.md).
